description: §23.2.4a no free lexical capture — a `_={ … }=` slice cannot see an enclosing scrml local it does not cross (`hidden`) nor a module-level scrml binding (`banner`). Probed with `typeof`, which reads an unbound name as "undefined" instead of throwing, so the observable is the slice's view of its own scope: the first slice crosses nothing and sees neither name; the second crosses `n` and sees `n` but still not `hidden`. Run as a `kind="tool"` program so the slice EXECUTES (a foreign slice is host code; its scope is a runtime property, not a diagnostic).
rationale: §23.2.4a crossing grammar: "The named values are the ONLY things that cross — there is NO free lexical capture (the slice sees only what `in:{}` names)." An implementation that lowers the slice in place (an in-process closure over the enclosing scope) prints "string,string" and "number,string" — the escape g-foreign-iife-captures-module-scope-s454 recorded, where the same leak reached the compiler's raw database handle. The seal removes scrml-scope and compiler-owned bindings only; host globals stay reachable (see foreign-slice-sealed-crossings-pos).
